title: What happens to the One left over when we divide by four?
description: One thousand three hundred and twenty five is shared into four equal groups by place value. The last One is regrouped into Tenths and then Hundredths, and an equal fraction checks the answer. Keeko's doubt is that the sharing stops at a remainder of one.
teaching_notes: One idea: a leftover One becomes ten Tenths, and the sharing goes on after the decimal point. Watch for students who stop at a remainder of one.

source: Find 1325 ÷ 4 by place value, and verify with an equivalent
video_script.why: The child can share Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones but has always stopped at a remainder.
video_script.substitution: One One is ten Tenths, and two Tenths are twenty Hundredths, so the sharing goes on.
video_script.anchor: One thousand three hundred and twenty five, shared into four equal groups
video_script.wrong_answer: three hundred and thirty one remainder one
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stops at three hundred and thirty one with a remainder of one, though the last One can be regrouped into Tenths.
video_script.payoff_line: The answer is three hundred and thirty one point two five.

final_answer.spoken: three hundred and thirty one point two five

video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 1325/4 is read one thousand three hundred and twenty five over four, and 33125/100 is read thirty three thousand one hundred and twenty five over a hundred.
maths_rules: 13 Hundreds / 4 = 3 Hundreds rem 1 Hundred; 12 Tens / 4 = 3 Tens
video_script.design: The place-value blocks stay on the board; the leftover One breaks into Tenths, then Hundredths, and an equal fraction checks the result.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; place-value blocks: 1 Thousand, 3 Hundreds, 2 Tens, 5 Ones above four empty groups

marks.num: the blocks appear above four empty groups
marks.chk: a fraction bar appears at the side
marks.ask: a question mark glows over one group

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book about sharing with place value.
<bookmark mark='num'/>The number is one thousand three hundred and twenty five, shared into four equal groups.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>The book checks the answer with an equal fraction.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much does each group get?

beats.on_screen: the blocks and the four groups stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: Th H T O columns; one block breaking into ten smaller blocks; a One breaking into ten Tenths

marks.blocks: the blocks sit in columns Thousands, Hundreds, Tens and Ones
marks.break: one block breaks into ten blocks of the next smaller place; the word regrouping is written
marks.tenths: a One breaks into ten Tenths, and a Tenth into ten Hundredths

narration: <bookmark mark='blocks'/>Look at the blocks, one Thousand, three Hundreds, two Tens and five Ones.
<bookmark mark='break'/>Breaking one block into ten smaller blocks is called regrouping.
<bookmark mark='tenths'/>A One can break into ten Tenths, and a Tenth can break into ten Hundredths.

beats.on_screen: Given: 1 Thousand + 3 Hundreds + 2 Tens + 5 Ones, shared into 4 equal groups

marks.given: the blocks and the four groups are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one Thousand, three Hundreds, two Tens and five Ones, to be shared into four equal groups.

beats.on_screen: To find: what each of the 4 groups gets, and check it with an equal fraction

marks.find: the share of one group and a check box are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much each group gets, and then check it.

beats.on_screen: 1 Thousand + 3 Hundreds = 13 Hundreds; 13 Hundreds ÷ 4: 3 Hundreds each, 1 Hundred remains; 1 Hundred + 2 Tens = 12 Tens; 12 Tens ÷ 4 = 3 Tens each

marks.s1a: the Thousand breaks into ten Hundreds and joins the three Hundreds
marks.s1b: three Hundreds go to each group and one Hundred remains
marks.s1c: the Hundred breaks into ten Tens and joins the two Tens, then three Tens go to each group

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the big places. Regroup the Thousand into ten Hundreds, and we have thirteen Hundreds.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Thirteen Hundreds divided by four gives three Hundreds each, and one Hundred remains.
<bookmark mark='s1c'/>Regroup that Hundred into ten Tens. With two Tens, that makes twelve Tens, and each group gets three Tens.

marks.s2b: one One goes to each group and one One remains

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, share the Ones. We have five Ones.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Five Ones divided by four gives each group one One, and one One remains.

beats.on_screen: 1 One = 10 Tenths; point placed; 10 Tenths ÷ 4 = 2 Tenths each, 2 Tenths remain; 2 Tenths = 20 Hundredths; 20 Hundredths ÷ 4 = 5 Hundredths each

marks.s3a: the last One breaks into ten Tenths and a decimal point is placed
marks.s3b: two Tenths go to each group and two Tenths remain
marks.s3c: the two Tenths break into twenty Hundredths and five go to each group

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, regroup the last One into ten Tenths. Put the decimal point in the answer.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Ten Tenths divided by four gives two Tenths each, and two Tenths remain.
<bookmark mark='s3c'/>Regroup them into twenty Hundredths. Twenty Hundredths divided by four gives five Hundredths each.

marks.s4b: 4 × 25 = 100 is marked, and top and bottom are multiplied by 25
marks.s4c: 33125/100 is written with the decimal left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Step four, check with an equal fraction. The division is one thousand three hundred and twenty five over four.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Four times twenty five is a hundred, so multiply the top and the bottom by twenty five.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>That gives thirty three thousand one hundred and twenty five over a hundred.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The answer is three hundred and thirty one point two five.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Place value and the equal fraction give the same answer.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the blocks
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 331 rem 1; the lone One block glows and is cut into ten thin Tenth strips; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the lone One block glows and is cut into ten Tenth strips
marks.right: the point is placed and the sharing goes on

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the answer is three hundred and thirty one remainder one.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the last One is still a block. It can be regrouped into ten Tenths, in the way that a Hundred became ten Tens.
<bookmark mark='right'/>The sharing goes on past the point, and a remainder is never the end.
